purpose: Follow possible observed counts into the probability that an interval covers a fixed teaching-model value.
meaning: A confidence procedure constructs intervals from data so that, under repeated sampling, a stated fraction cover a fixed parameter. This finite demonstration evaluates binomial coverage of two-sided 95% Clopper–Pearson intervals. At k=0 set L=0; at k=8 set U=1.

definition.setting: Eight independent packets either contain a bonus sticker or do not. Compute a two-sided 95% Clopper–Pearson interval for each possible count. A known teaching-model probability p lets us inspect coverage across all nine counts.
definition.formal_latex: K\sim\operatorname{Bin}(8,p),\quad\alpha=0.05.\quad L(0)=0,\quad U(8)=1,\quad P_{L(k)}(K\ge k)=\alpha/2\ (1\le k\le8),\quad P_{U(k)}(K\le k)=\alpha/2\ (0\le k\le7),\quad P_p\{L(K)\le p\le U(K)\}\ge0.95.

signature.p: Fixed probability used to inspect repeated-sampling coverage.
signature.k: Highlighted observed count out of eight.
signature.L(k): Lower endpoint of the highlighted interval.
signature.U(k): Upper endpoint of the highlighted interval.

conditions: Eight independent packets either contain a bonus sticker or do not. Compute a two-sided 95% Clopper–Pearson interval for each possible count. A known teaching-model probability p lets us inspect coverage across all nine counts.

The interval describes uncertainty about a fixed p, not a 95% posterior probability for p in one computed interval. Exact means binomial-tail inversion without a normal approximation; numeric endpoints use 70 bisections. Discreteness generally makes coverage greater than 95%.

prompts.prompt: At p=1/2, what probability belongs to intervals that cover p?
prompts.answer: At p=1/2 only counts 0 and 8 miss. Their combined chance is 2/256, so coverage is 254/256=0.9921875. Discreteness makes this conservative procedure exceed 95%; counting green rows without probability weights gives the wrong answer.
